answer: A sponsor carries 21% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. Because the saffron liability is written down in the pearl ledger at admission, the oasis audit exposes the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must as a result place its own capital behind each extra identity it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 6 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
